correctness.rationale: A direct renewal identity for each backbone crossing gives crossing mean m_i and variance recurrence v_0=m_0²+q(ℓ_0), v_i=v_(i-1)+m_(i-1)²+m_i²+q(ℓ_i); strong Markov independence yields the exact T variance. The length-L tooth second moment follows from finite Poisson equations, including the reflecting tip. Hölder with weights N-i gives an attainable cubic lower bound; integer rounding proves a matching O_N(M²) upper bound, strict convexity forces all limiting minimizers. The two-tooth forward difference is strictly increasing and odd, so unique optimum has the given closed form and the first transition occurs at M=3. The independent killed-generator checker verifies exact mean/variance for 169 small geometries; finite checks do not establish the infinite proof. No assumption of independent tooth excursions is used.

originality.rationale: The assessment concerns the constrained variance minimization theorem, not the well-established graph/tree mean or variance identities. Inspected full comb papers prove waiting-time/propagator relations and homogeneous-tooth results, but do not give the fixed total heterogeneous tooth budget optimum, its inverse-square-root allocation law, or the all-budget two-tooth threshold. Targeted semantic searches of published mathematical records and comparisons to all accessible local claim titles found no identical or stronger implication. The inaccessible 2011 general-tree full text and other broader literature leave genuine residual priority risk; this is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Fixing total reflecting branch length is a natural spatial material/resource constraint for a transport comb, and absorption-time dispersion quantifies reliability. Mean optimality uniquely deposits the full budget at the last site, but the variance optimum forces positive allocations at every site asymptotically, with a universal inverse-square-root law and sharp coefficient. In the minimal two-tooth model, the finite transition at M=3 quantifies the first unavoidable mean–variance tradeoff. This is a complete structural optimization result for a natural observable, not a routine moment calculation or isolated numeric case.
